components.note: 扌 (hand) — assembling things by hand
并 (bìng) means 'together' and gives a rough sound hint for pīn

example.hanzi: 我们把两张桌子拼在一起。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen bǎ liǎng zhāng zhuōzi pīn zài yìqǐ.
example.english: We pushed the two tables together.
example.fact: 拼 is to join pieces: 拼图 (jigsaw puzzle), 拼音 (Pinyin, literally "spell the sounds"), and 拼车 (to carpool). It also means to give it everything: 拼命 (to go all out), 拼搏 (to struggle hard).

components.note: 艹 (plant) — the tea plant
The lower 人 and 木 are conventionally read as a person among trees, a loose picture of picking tea

example.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng hē chá háishi hē kāfēi?
example.english: Would you like tea or coffee?
example.fact: Languages borrowed the word for tea from two Chinese sources: "chai" and "cha" trace back to Mandarin or Cantonese chá, while English "tea" comes from Min Chinese te via Dutch traders. In China 茶 can also mean tea-like infusions, such as 花茶 and 奶茶.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — an answer or agreement
隹 (zhuī) gives a loose sound hint for wéi

example.pinyin: Wéiyī de bànfǎ jiùshì děng.
example.english: The only way is to wait.
example.fact: 唯 is a bound form in written Chinese: 唯一 (the only), 唯有 (only), 唯独 (solely). It is pronounced exactly like 维 and 惟 (also wéi), which is why 惟一 is sometimes seen as a variant of 唯一.

components.note: 车 (vehicle) — the old 輕 first named a light chariot
工 and 又 together are a simplified stand-in for 巠 (jīng) in 輕, which gave the sound

example.pinyin: Tā qīngqīng de guān shàng le mén.
example.english: She closed the door gently.
example.fact: 轻 means light in weight (the opposite of 重) and gentle in action: 轻轻地. It also gives 轻松 (relaxed, at ease), 年轻 (young) and 轻视 (to look down on).

components.note: Likely a drawing of a bent arm or elbow, borrowed for the number nine; the origin is debated

example.pinyin: Xiànzài shì zǎoshang jiǔ diǎn.
example.english: It is nine in the morning.
example.fact: 九 sounds like 久 (jiǔ, long-lasting), which makes it auspicious, and as the largest single digit it stood for the emperor in 九五之尊. The Double Ninth Festival (重阳节) falls on the ninth day of the ninth lunar month.

components.note: Simplified form of 擊; the complex upper part of the old shape is replaced by a short stroke

example.hanzi: 足球队在比赛中击败了对手。
example.pinyin: Zúqiúduì zài bǐsài zhōng jībài le duìshǒu.
example.english: The football team beat its opponent in the match.
example.fact: 击 is mostly a bound form: 攻击 (to attack), 打击 (a blow, a setback), 射击 (to shoot), 击败 (to defeat). 点击 (to click) is the everyday computer verb.

components.note: Simplified form of 龍, which pictured a long, horned, coiling creature; the modern shape keeps only a hint of it

example.pinyin: Lóng shì Zhōngguó wénhuà de xiàngzhēng.
example.english: The dragon is a symbol of Chinese culture.
example.fact: Chinese 龙 are not fire-breathing monsters: they are benevolent water and rain spirits and an imperial emblem. 龙年 is the Year of the Dragon, and 望子成龙 means to hope one's son will become a dragon, i.e. a success.

components.note: 土 (earth) — burying uses earth
里 (lǐ) gives a loose sound hint for mái

example.pinyin: Gǒu bǎ gǔtou mái zài dìxià.
example.english: The dog buried the bone underground.
example.fact: 埋 is mái when it means to bury (埋头 "to bury one's head", to be absorbed in work) but mán in 埋怨 (to complain). The same verb is used for burying both objects and feelings: 埋藏.

components.note: Simplified form of 蓋; the 羊 over 皿 shape is a reduction, not a sheep on a dish

example.pinyin: Qǐng gài shang gàizi.
example.english: Please put the lid on.
example.fact: 盖 covers things in several ways: a lid (盖子), to put on a cover (盖被子, pull up the quilt), to stamp (盖章), and in everyday speech to build a house: 盖房子. Related words are 锅盖 (pot lid) and 盖饭 (rice with a topping).

components.note: 角 (horn) — the animal horn
刀 (knife) and 牛 (ox) — a knife taking an ox's horn apart, the old picture of dissecting

example.hanzi: 我不理解这个词的意思。
example.pinyin: Wǒ bù lǐjiě zhège cí de yìsi.
example.english: I don't understand the meaning of this word.
example.fact: 解 grew from taking apart to solving and understanding: 解决 (to solve), 解释 (to explain), 了解 (to know about), 理解 (to comprehend). It is xiè in the surname 解 (Xiè).

components.note: A drawing of two interlocking teeth, which is why the character looks jagged

example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān shuā liǎng cì yá.
example.english: I brush my teeth twice a day.
example.fact: 牙 is the everyday word for tooth: 刷牙 (brush teeth), 牙医 (dentist), 拔牙 (pull a tooth). The formal word is 牙齿, and 象牙 is ivory (literally elephant tooth).

components.note: 门 (gate) — an enclosing doorway
市 (market) — a market inside the gate, the picture of a noisy crowd

example.pinyin: Wàimiàn tài nào le, wǒ shuì bu zháo.
example.english: It's too noisy outside, I can't sleep.
example.fact: 闹 is noisy, but 热闹 (rènao) is "lively" in a good way, since noise is a sign of a happy festival or gathering. It also appears in 闹钟 (alarm clock), 闹笑话 (to make a fool of oneself) and 闹肚子 (to have an upset stomach).

components.note: 氵 (water) — water makes things slippery
骨 (gǔ) gives a loose sound hint for huá

example.pinyin: Dìshang hěn huá, xiǎoxīn diǎn.
example.english: The floor is slippery, be careful.
example.fact: 滑 describes slippery or smooth surfaces and the action of sliding: 滑雪 (skiing), 滑冰 (skating), 滑板 (skateboard), 光滑 (smooth). 滑稽 (huájī) means comical.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — dew is moisture from the sky
路 (lù) gives the sound exactly

example.pinyin: Tā lù chū le xiàoróng.
example.english: He broke into a smile.
example.fact: 露 means dew and, by extension, to expose: 暴露 (to expose), 露营 (camping), 露天 (open-air). In casual speech the verb is often read lòu: 露面 (to show up), 露馅 (to let the secret out).

components.note: 扌 (hand) — touching is done by hand
莫 (mò) gives the sound; mō is close

example.pinyin: Qǐng búyào mō xiǎogǒu.
example.english: Please don't touch the puppy.
example.fact: 摸 is to touch or feel for something, and it extends to finding things out: 摸清 (to figure out). 摸索 (to grope, to explore) and the slang 摸鱼 (to slack off at work, literally "to catch fish") are common.

components.note: 木 (wood) — a wooden board
反 (fǎn) gives the sound; bǎn is close

example.pinyin: Lǎoshī zài hēibǎn shang xiě zì.
example.english: The teacher writes on the blackboard.
example.fact: 板 is a flat piece: 黑板 (blackboard), 木板 (plank), 滑板 (skateboard). 老板 (lǎobǎn) means boss or shop owner, and 板着脸 means to keep a stern straight face.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water waves
皮 (pí) gives a loose sound hint for bō

example.pinyin: Hǎi lǐ yǒu hěn dà de bōlàng.
example.english: There are big waves in the sea.
example.fact: 波 is a wave in water and, by extension, in physics and in trouble: 电波 (radio wave), 风波 (disturbance), 一波三折 (many twists). It is also used in transliterations like 波兰 (Poland) and 波士顿 (Boston).

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — body fat
半 (bàn) gives a rough sound hint for pàng

example.pinyin: Tā zuìjìn yǒudiǎn pàng le.
example.english: He has put on a bit of weight lately.
example.fact: 胖 is blunt: calling someone 胖 can be rude, so politer speakers say 微胖 (a little chubby) or 丰满. For babies and pets, though, 胖乎乎 is a cute word for plump. The old reading pán survives only in the idiom 心宽体胖.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words used to name or acknowledge
人 (rén) gives the sound; rèn is close

example.pinyin: Wǒ rènshi tā hěn duō nián le.
example.english: I have known him for many years.
example.fact: 认 appears in 认识 (to know someone), 认为 (to think, to consider), 认真 (serious, earnest), 承认 (to admit). 认识 is for people and places you are acquainted with, whereas 知道 is for facts.

components.note: 革 (leather) — the bridle was made of leather
力 (lì) gives a loose sound hint for the lè/lēi readings

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ shéngzi lēi de hěn jǐn.
example.english: He pulled the rope very tight.
example.fact: 勒 is lēi when it means pulling something tight (勒紧裤带, to tighten one's belt, a figure for economizing) but lè in 勒索 (to extort) and 勒令 (to order). The idiom 悬崖勒马 means to rein in the horse at the cliff edge, i.e. stop before it is too late.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hitting is done by hand
奏 (zòu) gives the sound exactly

example.pinyin: Tā bèi bàba zòu le yí dùn.
example.english: His dad gave him a beating.
example.fact: 揍 is the casual, tough word for beating someone up, with 顿 as the measure word: 揍了一顿. 欠揍 means "asking for a beating". It is stronger than the neutral 打.

components.note: 犭 (dog) — a canine animal
良 (liáng) gives the sound; láng is close

example.pinyin: Shān lǐ yǒu láng.
example.english: There are wolves in the mountains.
example.fact: Wolves in Chinese idioms stand for greed and cruelty: 狼心狗肺 (heartless), 引狼入室 (to invite a wolf into the house), 狼吞虎咽 (to wolf down food). The measure word is 只 or 头.

components.note: 木 (wood) — wooden moulds for casting
莫 (mò) gives the sound; mó is close

example.hanzi: 这个孩子在模仿大人说话。
example.pinyin: Zhège háizi zài mófǎng dàrén shuōhuà.
example.english: The child is imitating how adults talk.
example.fact: 模 is mó in 模仿 (imitate), 模型 (model), 模特 (fashion model) and 规模 (scale). It is read mú in 模样 (appearance) and 模子 (mould).

components.note: A relatively late character with no clear ancient origin; the shape is often read as 用 with a flicking stroke

example.pinyin: Tā shuǎi le shuǎi tóufa.
example.english: He tossed his hair.
example.fact: 甩 is to swing or fling: 甩手 (to swing the arms), 甩头 (to toss the head). It extends to getting rid of: 甩掉 (to shake off), 被甩了 (to be dumped). 甩手掌柜 is a boss who delegates everything.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — inserting by hand
臿 (chā) gives the sound exactly

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ chātóu chā jìn chāzuò.
example.english: Please plug the plug into the socket.
example.fact: 插 is to push something in: 插头 (plug), 插座 (socket), 插花 (flower arranging). It also means to cut in: 插嘴 (to interrupt), 插队 (to jump the queue).

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement
云 (yún) gives the sound; yùn is close

example.pinyin: Wǒmen yòng kǎchē yùn huò.
example.english: We transport goods by truck.
example.fact: 运 means to carry and move: 运输 (transport), 运动 (exercise). It also means luck or fate: 运气, 好运, 命运. 运气 makes it clear whether luck is good or bad.

components.note: 日 (sun) — brightness from the sun
月 (moon) — brightness from the moon; together they say 'bright'

example.pinyin: Míngtiān huì gèng hǎo.
example.english: Tomorrow will be better.
example.fact: 明 means bright and by extension clear: 明白 (to understand), 明确 (clear), 明显 (obvious). 明天 (tomorrow) is literally "bright day". 明 is also the Ming dynasty (1368–1644).

components.note: Old form shows a hand holding a recording tool, the scribe who kept records, hence 'history'

example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan dú Zhōngguó lìshǐ.
example.english: I like reading Chinese history.
example.fact: 史 is mostly in compounds: 历史 (history), 史书 (history book), 史前 (prehistoric), 史无前例 (unprecedented). 《史记》 (Records of the Grand Historian) by Sima Qian is the model for later Chinese histories.

components.note: 女 (woman) — a girl
尼 (ní) gives the sound; nī is close

example.pinyin: Nīni shì wǒ de xiǎo zhínǚ.
example.english: Nini is my little niece.
example.fact: 妮 is found in girls' names and nicknames, often doubled as 妮妮, and in transliterations such as 安妮 (Anne) or 妮可 (Nicole). Northern dialect also uses 妮子 for "girl".

excludeSuggestion: Occurs almost only in personal names and transliterations

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — the old character 勝 was linked to strength
生 (shēng) gives the sound; shèng is close

example.pinyin: Wǒmen duì yǐ sān bǐ yī huòshèng.
example.english: Our team won three to one.
example.fact: 胜 is to win: 胜利 (victory), 战胜 (to overcome), 获胜 (to win). It also means to surpass: 一个比一个强, 胜于. 名胜 means a famous scenic spot, and 数不胜数 means countless.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — early boxes and carts were of bamboo
相 (xiāng) gives the sound exactly

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ xíngli fàng jìn xiāngzi lǐ.
example.english: Please put the luggage in the box.
example.fact: 箱 makes many container words: 冰箱 (fridge), 行李箱 (suitcase), 信箱 (mailbox), 邮箱 (email inbox, or an email address). 箱子 is the general word for a box or suitcase.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — tasting
未 (wèi) gives the sound exactly

example.pinyin: Zhè dào cài de wèidào hěn hǎo.
example.english: This dish tastes very good.
example.fact: 味 means taste or smell, and 味道 covers both: 有味道 can mean "flavourful" or "smelly". It builds 口味 (taste preference) and 五味 (the five tastes). In traditional medicine 味 counts herbs: 一味药 (one ingredient).

components.note: 雨 (rain) — a person waiting for the rain to pass, the old sense of 'to wait'
而 (ér) is the figure standing under the rain; later 'to need' grew from the idea of waiting

example.pinyin: Nǐ xūyào bāngzhù ma?
example.english: Do you need help?
example.fact: 需 is mostly in 需要 (to need, a need) and 需求 (demand). 需要 can act as a verb or a noun, unlike 要, which is a general "to want".

components.note: 亻 (person) — the human body
本 (běn) gives only a loose sound hint for tǐ

example.pinyin: Duànliàn shēntǐ hěn zhòngyào.
example.english: Exercising is very important.
example.fact: 体 is the simplified form of 體 and builds 身体 (body), 体育 (physical education), 体重 (weight), 体验 (experience). The same shape once served as an old variant of 笨 (bèn, clumsy), which is why 体 looks like 本 with a person.

components.note: 手 (hand) — two hands folded in greeting; the shape is made of 手 written twice

example.hanzi: 过年的时候我们去拜年。
example.pinyin: Guònián de shíhou wǒmen qù bàinián.
example.english: At New Year we go to pay New Year visits.
example.fact: 拜 is a respectful gesture: 拜年 (to pay New Year calls), 拜访 (to visit), 崇拜 (to worship), 拜托 (a polite "I'd be grateful if you'd"). 拜拜 is the casual "bye-bye".

components.note: 女 (woman) — the bride
昏 (hūn) gives the sound exactly; it means dusk, when ancient weddings were held

example.pinyin: Tāmen de hūnlǐ zài chūntiān.
example.english: Their wedding is in spring.
example.fact: 婚 is a bound form: 结婚 (to marry), 婚礼 (wedding), 离婚 (to divorce), 订婚 (to get engaged). Its sound part 昏 means dusk, because ritual weddings in ancient China were held at nightfall.

components.note: Origin debated; the upper shape looks like 高 (tall), suggesting a high place catching light

example.pinyin: Tiān liàng le, wǒmen chūfā ba.
example.english: It's light, let's set off.
example.fact: 亮 is both an adjective (bright) and a verb (to light up): 天亮 (daybreak), 亮灯 (turn on a light), 亮相 (to make an appearance). 漂亮 (piàoliang, pretty) and 响亮 (loud and clear) are common compounds.

components.note: 石 (stone) — brittle things shatter into pieces
卒 (zú) gives a loose sound hint for suì

example.pinyin: Bēizi diào zài dìshang suì le.
example.english: The cup fell and shattered.
example.fact: 碎 describes shattered or crushed things: 碎片 (fragment), 粉碎 (smash), 碎纸 (shredded paper). At New Year, a broken dish is waved off with 岁岁平安, because 碎 and 岁 (suì, year) sound the same.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — a vessel
般 (bān) gives a loose sound hint for pán

example.pinyin: Zhuōzi shang yǒu yì pán shuǐguǒ.
example.english: There is a plate of fruit on the table.
example.fact: 盘 is a plate or tray and the measure word for plated dishes: 一盘菜. It also counts games and records: 一盘棋 (a game of chess). 光盘 is a CD, and 盘点 means to take stock.

components.note: Simplified form of 圖; the 囗 frame still encloses a small picture

example.pinyin: Qǐng kàn zhè zhāng dìtú.
example.english: Please look at this map.
example.fact: 图 is a picture or plan: 地图 (map), 图片 (picture), 图书馆 (library, "picture-book hall"). As a verb it means to seek: 图方便 (to go for convenience), and 试图 means to attempt.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — an agreement made in words
丁 (dīng) gives the sound; dìng is close

example.hanzi: 我想订一张去北京的机票。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng dìng yì zhāng qù Běijīng de jīpiào.
example.english: I'd like to book a flight ticket to Beijing.
example.fact: 订 is to book or order: 订票, 订餐, 订阅 (to subscribe). It also means to fix an agreement: 订婚 (to get engaged), 订合同 (to sign a contract). Don't confuse it with 定 (dìng, to settle).

components.note: 大 (adult) — a standing grown man
一 (a hairpin) — a pin through the hair, the sign of adulthood in ancient China

example.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi hǎo zhàngfu.
example.english: He is a good husband.
example.fact: 夫 is rarely free-standing but common in compounds: 夫妻 (married couple), 丈夫 (husband), 夫人 (madam), 功夫 (kung fu). 大夫 is read dàifu (doctor) when colloquial and dàfū (a senior official) in history.

components.note: 贝 (shell) — money
弗 (fú) gives the sound; fèi is close

example.pinyin: Zhège yuè de shuǐdiànfèi hěn guì.
example.english: This month's water and electricity bill is expensive.
example.fact: 费 means both a fee and spending: 学费 (tuition), 免费 (free of charge), 浪费 (to waste), 小费 (tip). 费劲 means to take much effort. It is also a surname (Fèi).

components.note: 氵 (water) — a river
可 (kě) gives the sound; hé is close

example.pinyin: Hé lǐ yǒu hěn duō yú.
example.english: There are many fish in the river.
example.fact: 河 was originally the proper name of the Yellow River (黄河), while 江 was the Yangtze. Now it means any river, with the measure word 条, and appears in 银河 (the Milky Way, "silver river").

components.note: Origin debated; the hooked stroke over 口 (mouth) is usually taken to mean someone giving orders to manage an office

example.pinyin: Tā zài yì jiā xiǎo gōngsī gōngzuò.
example.english: He works at a small company.
example.fact: 司 is a bound form: 公司 (company), 司机 (driver), 司法 (judiciary), 上司 (boss). Its original sense is to take charge of something.

components.note: 亻 (person) — the old shape showed a person carrying a child on the back, a picture of protecting
呆 (dāi) is a worn-down shape here and gives only a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎohù hǎo nǐ de yǎnjing.
example.english: Please protect your eyes.
example.fact: 保 forms 保护 (to protect), 保证 (to guarantee), 保险 (insurance), 保持 (to keep, maintain) and 保安 (security guard). 请多保重 is a warm farewell meaning "please take good care of yourself".

meanings: measure word for doors and windows

components.note: 户 (door) — a door leaf
羽 (feather) — a thing that swings and flaps like a wing

example.pinyin: Fángjiān lǐ yǒu yí shàn dà chuānghu.
example.english: There is a big window in the room.
example.fact: 扇 is the measure word for doors and windows: 一扇门, 一扇窗. As a noun 扇子 is a hand fan, and the verb "to fan" is read shān: 扇风, 扇耳光 (to slap someone's face).

components.note: 见 (see) — perceiving
⺍ and 冖 are the shared top of 學 (to learn) — awareness as learning to see

example.pinyin: Wǒ juéde yǒudiǎn lěng.
example.english: I feel a bit cold.
example.fact: 觉得 (juéde) is the everyday way to say "I feel / I think" and softens opinions: 我觉得很好. The same character is read jiào in 睡觉 (to sleep) and 午觉 (nap), a classic reading pair. 感觉 means feeling.

components.note: 石 (stone) — an axe or stone blade
欠 (qiàn) gives a loose sound hint for kǎn

example.pinyin: Tā yòng fǔtóu kǎn shù.
example.english: He chops the tree down with an axe.
example.fact: 砍 is to chop with a blade: 砍柴 (to chop firewood), 砍树 (to fell a tree). In shopping slang 砍价 means to haggle the price down, and online sellers have turned this into group "price cutting" in apps.

components.note: Origin debated; the shape of a balanced bar with marks either side conveys 'level and even'

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù hěn píng.
example.english: This road is very flat.
example.fact: 平 means flat, level and by extension calm: 和平 (peace), 平安 (safe and sound), 平均 (average), 平时 (usually). 水平 is the level of an ability, as in 汉语水平 (Chinese level).
